questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: For PCl₅(g) ⇌ PCl₃(g) + Cl₂(g), which statement describes the equilibrium shift when pressure is decreased by expansion at fixed temperature?
questions.ai_explanation: The product side has two moles of gas for each mole on the reactant side. Expansion at fixed temperature lowers pressure and favours the products, increasing the equilibrium amount of PCl₃.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: The Arrhenius equation relates a reaction’s rate constant to temperature and its
questions.ai_explanation: The Arrhenius equation is k = A exp(−Eₐ/RT). It relates the rate constant to activation energy and temperature, with A the pre-exponential factor. At fixed A and T, a lower activation energy gives a larger rate constant.
questions.explanation: The Arrhenius equation is k = A exp(−Eₐ/RT). It relates the rate constant to activation energy and temperature, with A the pre-exponential factor. At fixed A and T, a lower activation energy gives a larger rate constant.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which description gives the thermal effect when NaOH flakes dissolve in water?
questions.ai_explanation: Dissolving sodium hydroxide releases heat overall because hydration of its ions releases more energy than is needed to separate the solid lattice. The solution warms, so the change is exothermic.
questions.explanation: Dissolving sodium hydroxide releases heat overall because hydration of its ions releases more energy than is needed to separate the solid lattice. The solution warms, so the change is exothermic.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Water vapour changes anhydrous cobalt(II) chloride from

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: At 20 °C, a salt of molar mass 101 g mol⁻¹ has solubility 0.34 mol dm⁻³. If 3.40 g dissolves in 250 cm³ of water with negligible volume change, the solution is

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: 25 cm³ of 0.2 mol dm⁻³ Na₂CO₃ requires 20 cm³ of HCl for complete neutralisation. What is the HCl concentration?
questions.ai_explanation: Na₂CO₃ + 2HCl → 2NaCl + H₂O + CO₂. The carbonate amount is 0.025 × 0.2 = 0.005 mol, requiring 0.010 mol HCl. The acid concentration is 0.010/0.020 = 0.50 mol dm⁻³.

questions.subject: chemistry

questions.question: Three drops of 1.0 mol dm⁻³ NaOH are added to 20 cm³ of an aqueous solution at pH 8.4. The resulting pH will be

questions.question: Neon and the heavier noble gases owe their low reactivity largely to their

questions.question: According to kinetic theory, increasing absolute temperature causes average kinetic energy of gas particles to
questions.ai_explanation: Mean translational kinetic energy of gas particles is proportional to absolute temperature: average Eₖ = 3kT/2. Increasing temperature therefore increases their average kinetic energy.

questions.subject: chemistry

questions.question: For an equilibrium whose forward reaction has ΔH > 0, which temperature change favours the forward equilibrium direction?

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: The defining feature of an anode reaction is that

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which quantity changes when a catalyst provides an alternative pathway?

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: If Y is an oxidizing agent that reacts with a reducing agent, Z, which of the following is correct?

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: In electrolysis of concentrated aqueous NaCl with inert electrodes, which pair represents cathode and anode discharge respectively in introductory ion-discharge notation?

questions.question: For CO(g) + H₂O(g) → CO₂(g) + H₂(g), calculate ΔH° using formation enthalpies CO₂(g) = −394, H₂O(g) = −242 and CO(g) = −110 kJ mol⁻¹.

questions.question: Which listed sample conducts electricity through mobile ions under the stated conditions?

options.D: It gives a white precipitate with acidified barium chloride

questions.explanation: With land and capital fixed, extra workers eventually have less fixed equipment and space per person. Beyond a point, each additional worker adds less output: diminishing marginal returns. Total output may still increase.

questions.subject: economics
questions.question: Which of the following best describes a production function?

options.C: It relates physical outputs to physical inputs

questions.subject: economics

options.B: All savings deposits in all banks during the year
options.C: All savings and time deposits in all banks during the year
options.D: The value of inventory change for the year

questions.question: Economic development differs from economic growth because the former

options.A: The allocation of resources to various sectors of the economy
options.B: The objectives of even distribution of income and wealth

questions.subject: economics
questions.question: The basic economic problems of the society include

options.A: What to produce, how and for whom
options.C: Scarcity, when to produce and how
options.D: Scarcity, for whom to produce and where

questions.explanation: Every economy chooses what to produce, how to produce it and who receives the output. These allocation decisions arise because resources are scarce.
questions.ai_explanation: Every economy chooses what to produce, how to produce it and who receives the output. These allocation decisions arise because resources are scarce.

questions.subject: economics
questions.question: Opportunity cost is an economic concept describing the

options.A: Monetary equivalent of the utility of a commodity
options.B: Amount of time or money invested in a commodity
options.C: Sacrifice made for the satisfaction of a want
options.D: Cost of retaining an optimum level of production of commodities

questions.explanation: Opportunity cost is the next-best alternative sacrificed to satisfy a chosen want. It measures the forgone opportunity rather than merely the money spent.
questions.ai_explanation: Opportunity cost is the next-best alternative sacrificed to satisfy a chosen want. It measures the forgone opportunity rather than merely the money spent.

questions.subject: economics
questions.question: The circular flow of income defines the

options.A: Relationship between ends and means in the economic system
options.B: Allocation of income to household members
options.C: Flow of goods, services and money among economic sectors

questions.explanation: Circular flow links real exchanges with corresponding money payments between sectors. It connects production, income and expenditure in the economy.
questions.ai_explanation: Circular flow links real exchanges with corresponding money payments between sectors. It connects production, income and expenditure in the economy.

questions.subject: economics
questions.question: The necessity of choice is due to the fact that
questions.explanation: Human wants are numerous and recurring, while the resources available to satisfy them are limited. People therefore have to choose which wants to satisfy first; choosing one use of a scarce resource means giving up another use.
questions.ai_explanation: Human wants are numerous and recurring, while the resources available to satisfy them are limited. People therefore have to choose which wants to satisfy first; choosing one use of a scarce resource means giving up another use.

options.B: The government acting in the interest of the country
options.C: The market women, the labour unions and the employers' association
options.D: Private individuals, organisations and the government

questions.question: If the actual population in a country is less than the optimum population, then

options.A: It is desirable to have a large population
options.B: It is necessary to have an improved technol ogy to sustain the population
options.C: It is desirable to have smaller population
options.D: The available resources are inadequate to sustain the population

questions.explanation: Total revenue is price multiplied by quantity. The four revenue totals are N75, N80, N85 and N90. Each additional unit adds N5, so marginal revenue, the change in total revenue divided by the change in quantity, is N5.

questions.subject: economics
questions.question: Elasticity of demand is an effective tool in the hands of a producer in that it enables him

options.A: Raise his profits and lowers his cost
options.D: Set his price to maximize his profit

questions.explanation: Price elasticity indicates how strongly quantity demanded responds to a price change. A producer can use it alongside cost information to evaluate pricing decisions and pursue maximum profit. Elasticity alone does not lower production costs or determine the profit-maximising price.
questions.ai_explanation: Price elasticity indicates how strongly quantity demanded responds to a price change. questions.subject: economics
questions.question: Cross elasticity of demand can be mathematically expressed as the

options.A: Percentage change in quantity of commodity X divided by percentage change in quantity of commodity Y
options.B: Percentage change in quantity demanded divided by percentage change in price
options.C: Percentage change in quantity demanded of commodity X divided by percentage change in price of commodity Y
options.D: Percentage change in quantity demanded divided by percentage change in income

questions.explanation: Cross elasticity measures the response of demand for one good to a price change in another good: percentage change in quantity demanded of X divided by percentage change in the price of Y. It is usually positive for substitutes and negative for complements.
questions.ai_explanation: Cross elasticity measures the response of demand for one good to a price change in another good: percentage change in quantity demanded of X divided by percentage change in the price of Y. It is usually positive for substitutes and negative for complements.

questions.subject: economics
questions.question: Output restriction, price setting and obstacles to free entry into the market are features of which market structure?
questions.explanation: A pure monopolist is the sole supplier in a market protected by barriers to entry. It can choose an output level and charge the corresponding price on the market demand curve. It cannot independently choose any price and any quantity it wishes.
questions.ai_explanation: A pure monopolist is the sole supplier in a market protected by barriers to entry. It can choose an output level and charge the corresponding price on the market demand curve. It cannot independently choose any price and any quantity it wishes.

questions.subject: economics
questions.question: The major factor that causes fluctuations in the supply of agricultural produce is
questions.explanation: Weather variations change rainfall, temperature and growing conditions, which directly affect crop yields and the amount available for sale. questions.subject: economics
questions.question: The system of agricultural practice which involves hunting, gathering and growing of food crops for family consumption only is described as
questions.explanation: Subsistence production is primarily intended to meet the producer's or household's own consumption needs. The decisive clue is that the food is for family consumption only, rather than principally for sale to a market.

questions.subject: economics
questions.question: What is the term used to describe a policy aimed at promoting the local production of goods which are usually imported?
questions.explanation: Import substitution promotes domestic production of goods that were previously bought from abroad. Its immediate objective is to replace imports with locally produced goods, often through support for domestic industries.
questions.ai_explanation: Import substitution promotes domestic production of goods that were previously bought from abroad. Its immediate objective is to replace imports with locally produced goods, often through support for domestic industries.

questions.subject: economics
questions.question: An increase in both the legal reserve ratio and the discount rate has what effect on the quantity of money in circulation?

options.A: Increasing the quantity of money in circulation
options.B: Decreasing the quantity of money in circulation

questions.explanation: These are contractionary monetary measures in the standard banking model. A higher required reserve ratio restricts deposit expansion, while a higher discount rate makes central-bank borrowing more costly. Together they tend to restrain credit and money growth.
questions.ai_explanation: These are contractionary monetary measures in the standard banking model. A higher required reserve ratio restricts deposit expansion, while a higher discount rate makes central-bank borrowing more costly. Together they tend to restrain credit and money growth.

questions.subject: economics
questions.question: Gresham's law states that

options.A: Good money drives out bad money
options.B: Bad money drives out good money
options.C: The value of money varies inversely with the price level
options.D: Gold must be available to maintain the value of paper money

questions.explanation: When two forms of money must circulate at the same legal value despite different intrinsic values, people tend to spend the overvalued money and retain, melt or export the undervalued money. In that setting, bad money drives good money out of circulation.
questions.ai_explanation: When two forms of money must circulate at the same legal value despite different intrinsic values, people tend to spend the overvalued money and retain, melt or export the undervalued money. In that setting, bad money drives good money out of circulation.

questions.subject: economics
questions.question: Monetary policy aimed at reducing demand-pull inflation in the country may be carried out through

options.A: Increase in taxation of private companies, public corporation and private individuals
options.B: Increase in cash reserve ratio of commercial banks and the sales of government securities
options.C: Decrease in government expenditure on education
options.D: Direct price control in the market place

questions.explanation: Increasing reserve requirements and selling government securities are contractionary monetary instruments. They restrain bank credit or withdraw liquidity, helping to reduce aggregate demand. Changes to taxes and government spending are fiscal measures, while direct price controls are administrative measures.
questions.ai_explanation: Increasing reserve requirements and selling government securities are contractionary monetary instruments. questions.subject: economics
questions.question: Progressive tax structure is designed to

options.A: Take more from the income of the poor
options.B: Take more from the income of the rich
options.C: Take equal proportion of income from both the rich and the poor
options.D: Reduce the problems emanating from tax impositon

questions.explanation: Under a progressive tax, the proportion of income paid in tax rises as income rises. Higher-income earners therefore bear a larger percentage burden, not merely a larger cash payment under an otherwise identical flat percentage rate.
questions.ai_explanation: Under a progressive tax, the proportion of income paid in tax rises as income rises. Higher-income earners therefore bear a larger percentage burden, not merely a larger cash payment under an otherwise identical flat percentage rate.

questions.subject: economics
questions.question: Taxes and government expenditures are instruments of
questions.explanation: Fiscal policy uses government taxation and expenditure to influence economic activity and resource allocation. Monetary policy instead concerns instruments such as interest rates, money and credit conditions, generally administered by the monetary authority.
questions.ai_explanation: Fiscal policy uses government taxation and expenditure to influence economic activity and resource allocation. Monetary policy instead concerns instruments such as interest rates, money and credit conditions, generally administered by the monetary authority.

questions.subject: economics
questions.question: One of the ways by which the government can speed up economic development is through the

options.A: Increase in consumption pattern of the people

options.C: Increase in the rate of population growth so as to ensure that the country has a large labour force
options.D: Encourage of importation of raw materials to produce consumers goods

questions.subject: economics
questions.question: The main objective of the Economic Community of West African State is to

options.A: Establish a West African Development Bank
options.C: Introduce a common currency for the sub- region
options.D: Promote the free movement of persons, goods and services within the sub-region

questions.question: With a given level of money income, a consumer maximizes satisfaction from the consumption of goods and services when he

options.B: marginal utility derived from each good or service is increasing at the same rate

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: When a business incurs labours cost in installing a fixed asset, the cost is treated as
questions.ai_explanation: Labour directly attributable to bringing a fixed asset into working condition forms part of its cost. Installation labour is therefore added to the asset rather than expensed as routine wages.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: Malam Gambo bought a freezer for his shop costing N 10,500. In recording, he debited office expenses account and credited the bank account. What book keeping error has he committed?

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: The use of the folio in the ledger is for

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: Tanko’s account has debits: opening balance ₦5,000 and sales ₦10,000; credits: cash ₦3,000 and bank ₦6,500. What is the closing balance amount?
questions.ai_explanation: Debits total ₦5,000 + ₦10,000 = ₦15,000. Credits total ₦3,000 + ₦6,500 = ₦9,500. Their difference is a closing debit balance of ₦5,500.

questions.subject: accounts

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: Purchases are ₦20,000; sales ₦40,000; carriage inwards ₦5,000; carriage outwards ₦5,000; opening stock ₦10,000; closing stock ₦5,000. Find cost of goods sold.

questions.explanation: Cost of goods sold is opening stock plus purchases and carriage inwards, less closing stock: ₦10,000 + ₦20,000 + ₦5,000 − ₦5,000 = ₦30,000. Carriage outwards is a selling expense.

questions.question: Opening stock:3,000 units at ₦3; January purchases:15,000 at ₦3.50; February purchases:25,000 at ₦4. January sales:13,000 at ₦4.50; February sales:28,000 at ₦5. If closing stock is valued at ₦20,000, calculate gross profit at the end of February.
questions.ai_explanation: Sales total ₦198,500. Goods available cost ₦161,500; with the specified closing value ₦20,000, cost of sales is ₦141,500. Gross profit is ₦198,500 − ₦141,500 = ₦57,000.

questions.subject: accounts

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: Opening and closing accounts receivable are ₦8,000 and ₦15,000. Customer collections are ₦36,000. With no other receivable movements, find credit sales.
questions.ai_explanation: Opening receivables plus credit sales less collections equals closing receivables. Thus credit sales = ₦15,000 − ₦8,000 + ₦36,000 = ₦43,000.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: Club subscriptions: opening arrears₦40; closing arrears₦35; opening receipts in advance₦15; cash received₦2,560. With no closing advance, find subscription income.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: Ada contributes cash₦12,000, furniture₦18,000 and a vehicle₦70,000. Udo contributes cash₦10,000, a building₦5,000 and a computer₦135,000. Find total partnership capital.

questions.subject: accounts

questions.ai_explanation: The partnership appropriation account allocates profit among partners, including agreed interest and salaries. A sole trader has no profit allocation among multiple owners.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: Authorised nominal capital₦50million is divided into100million shares.80million shares are issued fully paid at₦0.60 each. What is each share’s nominal value?

questions.subject: accounts

questions.question: Sales are₦20,000 and cost of sales is₦15,000. Find gross profit margin.

questions.ai_explanation: B’s gross profit is ₦4,000 − (₦1,500 + ₦3,000 − ₦2,500) = ₦2,000. Its one-fifth share of ₦11,500 expenses is ₦2,300, leaving a net loss of ₦300.

questions.subject: accounts

questions.question: Assets: motor van₦3,600,premises₦5,000,bank₦1,650,stock₦4,800,cash₦250,debtors₦6,910. Liabilities: loan₦1,000 and creditors₦2,560. Find capital.

questions.explanation: Total sales equal cash received from sales and debtors plus the increase in receivables. Thus ₦153,000 + ₦6,800 − ₦5,600 = ₦154,200 for the period.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: The statement of affairs prepared from incomplete records can be described as

options.A: the summary of all the business transac tions of the trader ascertained by the accountant
options.B: a balance sheet at a particular date showing the assets and liabilities of the business
options.C: a schedule of all the business ventures entered into for the period to which the records relate
options.D: the statement that shows the profit or loss made during the period.

questions.ai_explanation: A statement of affairs lists assets and liabilities at a particular date when complete double-entry records are unavailable. The difference gives the proprietor’s capital.
questions.explanation: A statement of affairs lists assets and liabilities at a particular date when complete double-entry records are unavailable. The difference gives the proprietor’s capital.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: The contribution margin on a job is the

options.C: excess of sales revenue over variable costs
options.D: difference between fixed and variable costs.

questions.ai_explanation: Contribution is sales revenue less variable costs. It is the amount available to cover fixed costs and then contribute to profit; it is not itself net profit.
questions.explanation: Contribution is sales revenue less variable costs. It is the amount available to cover fixed costs and then contribute to profit; it is not itself net profit.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: Opening raw materials ₦46,800; closing raw materials ₦38,600; defective purchases returned ₦9,200; materials consumed ₦448,500. Find gross purchases for the period.
questions.ai_explanation: Consumption equals opening inventory plus purchases less returns and closing inventory. Rearranging gives purchases ₦448,500 − ₦46,800 + ₦9,200 + ₦38,600 = ₦449,500.
questions.explanation: Consumption equals opening inventory plus purchases less returns and closing inventory. Rearranging gives purchases ₦448,500 − ₦46,800 + ₦9,200 + ₦38,600 = ₦449,500.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: Opening raw materials ₦46,800; closing raw materials ₦38,600; defective purchases returned ₦9,200; materials consumed ₦448,500. Find the cost of materials available for use.
questions.ai_explanation: Materials available for use comprise those consumed plus those left at the end. Therefore ₦448,500 + ₦38,600 = ₦487,100, after accounting for purchase returns.
questions.explanation: Materials available for use comprise those consumed plus those left at the end. Therefore ₦448,500 + ₦38,600 = ₦487,100, after accounting for purchase returns.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: The limitations of the receipts and payments account arise mainly because of the reliance

options.A: cash movement as evidence of transaction
options.C: the capital account of the organization
options.D: the transaction papers as evidence of transaction

questions.ai_explanation: Receipts and payments accounts track cash movements. They omit non-cash adjustments and do not allocate every receipt or payment to the period in which income or expense arises.
questions.explanation: Receipts and payments accounts track cash movements. They omit non-cash adjustments and do not allocate every receipt or payment to the period in which income or expense arises.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: The trading account is to a sole trader what income and expenditure account is to a
questions.ai_explanation: A non-profit organisation uses an income and expenditure account to measure its period surplus or deficit. It serves a performance-reporting role for an organisation without profit distribution.
questions.explanation: A non-profit organisation uses an income and expenditure account to measure its period surplus or deficit. It serves a performance-reporting role for an organisation without profit distribution.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: Which identify an ordinary partnership? I: a business exists; II: partners carry it on in common; III: it has a profit-making purpose; IV: partners’ liability is limited.
questions.ai_explanation: An ordinary partnership involves people carrying on a business in common with a view to profit. Limited liability is not a necessary feature of that general partnership relationship.
questions.explanation: An ordinary partnership involves people carrying on a business in common with a view to profit. Limited liability is not a necessary feature of that general partnership relationship.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: When forming a partnership, new partners should record non-monetary assets on the new partnership’s books at

options.B: their historical costs when first used
options.C: their historical costs when first purchased by each new partner
options.D: the highest values practical so that future income tax deductions are maximized.

questions.ai_explanation: Assets contributed to a newly formed partnership are recorded at agreed current fair values. Those values measure the contribution rather than the partner’s old purchase cost.
questions.explanation: Assets contributed to a newly formed partnership are recorded at agreed current fair values. Those values measure the contribution rather than the partner’s old purchase cost.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: Umar and Ahmed have capital balances of ₦40,000 and ₦60,000 and share profit equally. Abdullahi contributes directly to the partnership for a one-third capital interest with no bonus. Find his contribution.
questions.ai_explanation: Existing capital totals ₦100,000. Let the contribution be x; a one-third interest requires x/(100,000 + x) = 1/3. Thus 2x = ₦100,000 and x = ₦50,000.
questions.explanation: Existing capital totals ₦100,000. Let the contribution be x; a one-third interest requires x/(100,000 + x) = 1/3. Thus 2x = ₦100,000 and x = ₦50,000.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: Dan and Baker have capitals ₦50,000 and ₦30,000, share profits in that ratio, and Baker receives an ₦8,000 salary. Interest on drawings is 6% annually. Dan drew ₦15,000; Baker drew ₦14,000 in four equal amounts on 31 March, 30 June, 30 September and 31 December. Annual net profit is ₦48,000 and goodwill write-off ₦5,000. Find Baker’s drawings interest.
questions.ai_explanation: Each quarterly drawing is ₦14,000/4 = ₦3,500. Interest applies for 9, 6, 3 and 0 months respectively: ₦3,500 × 6% × 18/12 = ₦315.
questions.explanation: Each quarterly drawing is ₦14,000/4 = ₦3,500. Interest applies for 9, 6, 3 and 0 months respectively: ₦3,500 × 6% × 18/12 = ₦315.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: The ordinary shareholders enjoy the following rights except the right to

options.C: participate in additional issues of shares
options.D: receive dividends at a predetermined rate.

questions.ai_explanation: Ordinary dividends depend on distributable profit and the dividend decision; they are not promised at a predetermined rate. Voting and participation rights differ from a fixed dividend entitlement.
questions.explanation: Ordinary dividends depend on distributable profit and the dividend decision; they are not promised at a predetermined rate. Voting and participation rights differ from a fixed dividend entitlement.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: Granada has net assets ₦600,000, contributed capital ₦180,000 and 30,000 ordinary shares with no preference shares. Which statement follows?
questions.ai_explanation: With no preference shares, the ₦600,000 net assets belong to ordinary shareholders. Divide by 30,000 shares to obtain book value of ₦20 per share.
questions.explanation: With no preference shares, the ₦600,000 net assets belong to ordinary shareholders. Divide by 30,000 shares to obtain book value of ₦20 per share.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: Which calculation gives the debt-to-equity form of gearing?
questions.ai_explanation: The debt-to-equity form of gearing compares long-term debt with equity capital. It indicates the extent of long-term borrowing relative to shareholders’ funding.
questions.explanation: The debt-to-equity form of gearing compares long-term debt with equity capital. It indicates the extent of long-term borrowing relative to shareholders’ funding.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: Udoh: capital ₦39,000; long-term loan ₦15,000; creditors ₦9,000; accrued wages ₦5,000; land ₦20,000; building ₦30,000; stock ₦4,000; cash ₦8,000; debtors ₦6,000. Find working capital.
questions.ai_explanation: Current assets are stock ₦4,000, cash ₦8,000 and debtors ₦6,000, totalling ₦18,000. Less creditors and accrued wages of ₦14,000 gives working capital ₦4,000.
questions.explanation: Current assets are stock ₦4,000, cash ₦8,000 and debtors ₦6,000, totalling ₦18,000. Less creditors and accrued wages of ₦14,000 gives working capital ₦4,000.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: Which of the following entries is effected by a department when goods are charged to it at selling prices?
questions.ai_explanation: Goods received increase the department’s stock. When inventory is maintained at selling price, the receiving stock account is debited at that price, with the loading handled separately.
questions.explanation: Goods received increase the department’s stock. When inventory is maintained at selling price, the receiving stock account is debited at that price, with the loading handled separately.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: Udoh: capital ₦39,000; long-term loan ₦15,000; creditors ₦9,000; accrued wages ₦5,000; land ₦20,000; building ₦30,000; stock ₦4,000; cash ₦8,000; debtors ₦6,000. Find the acid-test ratio.
questions.ai_explanation: Quick assets exclude stock: cash ₦8,000 plus debtors ₦6,000 equal ₦14,000. Current liabilities are also ₦14,000, giving an acid-test ratio of 1:1.
questions.explanation: Quick assets exclude stock: cash ₦8,000 plus debtors ₦6,000 equal ₦14,000. Current liabilities are also ₦14,000, giving an acid-test ratio of 1:1.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: The difference between the closure of the books of a branch and those of a separate company is that

options.A: there is retained earnings account on the branch books
options.B: the revenue and expense account is closed to branch current account
options.C: there is no retained earnings account on the branch books
options.D: the revenue and expense account is not closed to the home office current account

questions.ai_explanation: A branch forms part of the head-office entity and closes its result to the head-office account. It does not retain a separate company-style retained earnings account.
questions.explanation: A branch forms part of the head-office entity and closes its result to the head-office account. It does not retain a separate company-style retained earnings account.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: What does fiscal compliance mean?

options.A: All financial and related laws and regulations are adhered to
options.B: Only the current budget is complied with and no deficits allowed
options.C: All physical asset requirements have been met
options.D: Fiscal planning is necessary for proper public-sector accountability

questions.ai_explanation: Fiscal compliance means adhering to applicable financial laws and regulations. It covers more than avoiding a budget deficit or meeting physical asset requirements.
questions.explanation: Fiscal compliance means adhering to applicable financial laws and regulations. It covers more than avoiding a budget deficit or meeting physical asset requirements.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: Which are advantages of departmental accounts? I: identify the highest-profit department; II: easily calculate business capital; III: reveal sources of funding; IV: encourage healthy rivalry.
questions.ai_explanation: Departmental results identify the most profitable units and can encourage healthy comparison. They do not by themselves establish overall capital or reveal sources of funding.
questions.explanation: Departmental results identify the most profitable units and can encourage healthy comparison. They do not by themselves establish overall capital or reveal sources of funding.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: The end result of governmental accounting procedure is to

options.A: Keep proper records of government expenditure
options.B: Give financial information to the public and investors
options.C: Produce timely and accurate financial reports for legislators and the public
options.D: Give information on the performance of public enterprises

questions.ai_explanation: Government accounting produces timely, accurate financial reports for oversight and public accountability. Keeping transaction records supports that broader reporting outcome.
questions.explanation: Government accounting produces timely, accurate financial reports for oversight and public accountability. Keeping transaction records supports that broader reporting outcome.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: The basic role of accounting is to;
questions.ai_explanation: Accounting measures and communicates financial performance and position. Detecting fraud or protecting shareholders may benefit from accounting, but performance measurement is its basic role here.
questions.explanation: Accounting measures and communicates financial performance and position. Detecting fraud or protecting shareholders may benefit from accounting, but performance measurement is its basic role here.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: Bakery: opening stock ₦800; flour purchases ₦2,450; sales ₦4,745; bakery staff wages ₦675; carriage outwards ₦50; administrative salaries ₦225; closing stock ₦940; capital ₦1,540. Find cost of goods sold.
questions.ai_explanation: Cost of goods sold includes opening stock, flour purchases and bakery production wages, less closing stock: ₦800 + ₦2,450 + ₦675 − ₦940 = ₦2,985. Distribution and administration are excluded.
questions.explanation: Cost of goods sold includes opening stock, flour purchases and bakery production wages, less closing stock: ₦800 + ₦2,450 + ₦675 − ₦940 = ₦2,985. Distribution and administration are excluded.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: Petty-cash imprest is ₦1,380. Expenses: stationery ₦350, cleaning materials ₦335, general expenses ₦265. Find the reimbursement needed to restore the imprest.
questions.ai_explanation: Under the imprest system, reimbursement equals the supported expenses. Adding stationery ₦350, cleaning materials ₦335 and general expenses ₦265 gives ₦950.
questions.explanation: Under the imprest system, reimbursement equals the supported expenses. Adding stationery ₦350, cleaning materials ₦335 and general expenses ₦265 gives ₦950.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: Revenue ₦820,000; office rent ₦20,000; electricity ₦15,000; staff salaries ₦120,000; miscellaneous expenses 10% of revenue. Find net income for the year ended 30 June 2001.
questions.ai_explanation: Miscellaneous expenses are 10% of ₦820,000, or ₦82,000. Total expenses are ₦237,000, leaving net income ₦820,000 − ₦237,000 = ₦583,000.
questions.explanation: Miscellaneous expenses are 10% of ₦820,000, or ₦82,000. Total expenses are ₦237,000, leaving net income ₦820,000 − ₦237,000 = ₦583,000.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: When a proprietor withdraw cash from the business for private use, he

options.A: debits cash account and credits drawings account
options.B: credits cash account and debit its bank account
options.C: debits bank account and credit drawings account
options.D: credits cash account and debit drawings accounts.

questions.ai_explanation: Personal cash withdrawals reduce business cash and the proprietor’s capital interest. Debit drawings to record the withdrawal and credit cash to record the outflow.
questions.explanation: Personal cash withdrawals reduce business cash and the proprietor’s capital interest. Debit drawings to record the withdrawal and credit cash to record the outflow.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: An entry in a subsidiary book which does not form part of the double entry system is a
questions.ai_explanation: A memorandum entry records information without creating a debit-and-credit posting in the double-entry ledger. It differs from a journal entry that forms part of that system.
questions.explanation: A memorandum entry records information without creating a debit-and-credit posting in the double-entry ledger. It differs from a journal entry that forms part of that system.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: Opening cash ₦7,600; closing cash ₦9,200; total cash receipts ₦18,000. Find cash payments.
questions.ai_explanation: Opening cash plus receipts equals payments plus closing cash. Payments are ₦7,600 + ₦18,000 − ₦9,200 = ₦16,400 for the period.
questions.explanation: Opening cash plus receipts equals payments plus closing cash. Payments are ₦7,600 + ₦18,000 − ₦9,200 = ₦16,400 for the period.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: Discount allowed totals ₦230 and discount received ₦255 in the cash book. Which treatment is correct?

options.A: They must be balanced in the cash book and the difference taken to the debtors ledger,
options.B: they must be balanced in the cash, balance and the difference taken to the trial balance.
options.C: They should not be balanced in the cash book before being taken to the trial balance.
options.D: They should not appear in the trial balance a they were already either received or paid out.

questions.ai_explanation: Discount allowed and discount received are separate expense and income totals. Their columns are totalled independently and posted to separate accounts, rather than balanced against each other.
questions.explanation: Discount allowed and discount received are separate expense and income totals. Their columns are totalled independently and posted to separate accounts, rather than balanced against each other.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: Which of the following bank reconciliation items should not be added or subtracted from the bank statement balance to determine the adjusted cash balnce?

options.C: deposits in the mail not yet received by the bank
options.D: Bank error, charging a company for another company’s cheques.

questions.ai_explanation: Bank service charges are already reflected in the bank statement. They adjust the company’s cash book when unrecorded there, not the statement balance itself.
questions.explanation: Bank service charges are already reflected in the bank statement. They adjust the company’s cash book when unrecorded there, not the statement balance itself.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: A vehicle costs ₦20,000 and is depreciated at 5% per year using the reducing-balance method. Find its carrying value after three years.
questions.ai_explanation: Reducing-balance depreciation retains 95% of carrying value each year. After three years the value is ₦20,000 × 0.95³ = ₦17,147.50.
questions.explanation: Reducing-balance depreciation retains 95% of carrying value each year. After three years the value is ₦20,000 × 0.95³ = ₦17,147.50.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: Opening capital ₦307,000; closing capital ₦342,000; net profit ₦121,600; opening stock ₦98,800; purchases ₦706,000; carriage inwards ₦17,500; cost of goods sold ₦740,700; selling, general and administration expenses ₦526,000; discount received ₦9,650. Find closing stock.
questions.ai_explanation: Goods available cost ₦98,800 + ₦706,000 + ₦17,500 = ₦822,300. Subtract cost of goods sold ₦740,700 to obtain closing stock ₦81,600.
questions.explanation: Goods available cost ₦98,800 + ₦706,000 + ₦17,500 = ₦822,300. Subtract cost of goods sold ₦740,700 to obtain closing stock ₦81,600.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: Opening capital ₦307,000; closing capital ₦342,000; net profit ₦121,600; opening stock ₦98,800; purchases ₦706,000; carriage inwards ₦17,500; cost of goods sold ₦740,700; selling, general and administration expenses ₦526,000; discount received ₦9,650. Find gross profit.
questions.ai_explanation: Net profit equals gross profit plus discount received less expenses. Gross profit is therefore ₦121,600 + ₦526,000 − ₦9,650 = ₦637,950.
questions.explanation: Net profit equals gross profit plus discount received less expenses. Gross profit is therefore ₦121,600 + ₦526,000 − ₦9,650 = ₦637,950.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: Chibuike buys 36 notebooks at ₦10 each, receives a 5% trade discount and takes a further 1% cash discount. Find the payment.
questions.ai_explanation: The list total is 36 × ₦10 = ₦360. Apply the 5% trade discount first, then the 1% cash discount: ₦360 × 0.95 × 0.99 = ₦338.58.
questions.explanation: The list total is 36 × ₦10 = ₦360. Apply the 5% trade discount first, then the 1% cash discount: ₦360 × 0.95 × 0.99 = ₦338.58.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: The main features of the single entry system are that

options.A: books of accounts are not maintained and business relies only on bank statement
options.B: the journal records are absent and only the main ledger is kept
options.C: there are incomplete classifications and recording procedures
options.D: only credit sales transactions and credit purchases are recorded.

questions.ai_explanation: Single-entry records do not consistently record both aspects of every transaction. Their incomplete classification and recording require reconstruction to prepare full accounts.
questions.explanation: Single-entry records do not consistently record both aspects of every transaction. Their incomplete classification and recording require reconstruction to prepare full accounts.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: The principal function of a sales ledger control account is to

options.A: serve as internal check and provide quick information for the preparation of interim financial statements
options.B: serve as external check and provide quick information for the preparation of interim financial statements
options.C: provide quick information for the preparation of customers’ statements,
options.D: provide information for the control of salesmen’s activities

questions.ai_explanation: The control account independently summarises customer balances and provides a quick receivables total. This supports internal checking and preparation of interim financial statements.
questions.explanation: The control account independently summarises customer balances and provides a quick receivables total. This supports internal checking and preparation of interim financial statements.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: Opening purchases-ledger credit balances ₦40,000 and debit balances ₦1,000; purchases journal ₦500,000; returns outwards ₦50,000; cheques to suppliers ₦400,000; promissory notes to suppliers ₦30,000; discounts received ₦8,000; contra against sales ledger ₦2,000. Find the total of either side after balancing the purchases ledger control account.
questions.ai_explanation: The credit side consists of opening credit balances ₦40,000 plus credit purchases ₦500,000, giving ₦540,000. The debit side reaches the same total after the closing balance is inserted.
questions.explanation: The credit side consists of opening credit balances ₦40,000 plus credit purchases ₦500,000, giving ₦540,000. The debit side reaches the same total after the closing balance is inserted.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: Cash received from debtors ₦30,000; purchases ₦21,000; opening debtors ₦4,000; equipment bought ₦2,500; closing debtors ₦3,000. Find sales represented by the debtors account.
questions.ai_explanation: Credit sales equal collections plus closing debtors less opening debtors. Thus ₦30,000 + ₦3,000 − ₦4,000 = ₦29,000; purchases and equipment do not enter this calculation.
questions.explanation: Credit sales equal collections plus closing debtors less opening debtors. Thus ₦30,000 + ₦3,000 − ₦4,000 = ₦29,000; purchases and equipment do not enter this calculation.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: When the factory cost of production has been ascertained, manufactured goods are transferred to trading accounts by

options.A: debiting manufacturing account and crediting trading account
options.B: crediting sales account and debiting trading account
options.C: debiting sales account and crediting trading account
options.D: crediting manufacturing account and debiting trading account.

questions.ai_explanation: Completed production cost leaves the manufacturing account and enters the trading account. Credit manufacturing and debit trading for the same amount.
questions.explanation: Completed production cost leaves the manufacturing account and enters the trading account. Credit manufacturing and debit trading for the same amount.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: Lawal and Co makes blocks and sells to builders. In computing prime cost, which of the following costs would be considered appropriate?

options.C: Sales boys wages, cement and sand
options.D: carriage outwards, carriage inwards and cement.

questions.ai_explanation: Water and cement are direct block-making materials. Inward carriage forms part of their acquisition cost; outward carriage and sales staff wages are selling costs, not prime cost.
questions.explanation: Water and cement are direct block-making materials. Inward carriage forms part of their acquisition cost; outward carriage and sales staff wages are selling costs, not prime cost.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: The difference between the factory cost of production and prime cost production is
questions.ai_explanation: Factory production cost combines prime cost with factory overhead. Direct materials and labour are already part of prime cost, while selling expenses lie outside production.
questions.explanation: Factory production cost combines prime cost with factory overhead. Direct materials and labour are already part of prime cost, while selling expenses lie outside production.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: Receipts and payments account of a non-profit making organisation is principally a summary of the
questions.ai_explanation: The receipts and payments account summarises cash and bank transactions recorded in the cash book. It includes both capital and revenue cash movements.
questions.explanation: The receipts and payments account summarises cash and bank transactions recorded in the cash book. It includes both capital and revenue cash movements.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: Club opening debtors ₦150; cash sales ₦4,850; closing debtors ₦900; cash received from debtors ₦550. Find total club sales.
questions.ai_explanation: Credit sales are collections ₦550 plus closing debtors ₦900 less opening debtors ₦150 = ₦1,300. Add cash sales ₦4,850 to obtain total club sales ₦6,150.
questions.explanation: Credit sales are collections ₦550 plus closing debtors ₦900 less opening debtors ₦150 = ₦1,300. Add cash sales ₦4,850 to obtain total club sales ₦6,150.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: Goodwill can be valued in partnership when,
questions.ai_explanation: Retirement changes partners’ interests in the business. Goodwill may be valued to compensate the retiring partner for their share of the business’s established earning capacity.
questions.explanation: Retirement changes partners’ interests in the business. Goodwill may be valued to compensate the retiring partner for their share of the business’s established earning capacity.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: A partner contributes equipment originally costing ₦20,000 with accumulated depreciation ₦12,500. The partners agree on a value of ₦9,000. What amount is debited to equipment in the partnership books?
questions.ai_explanation: The partnership records the asset at the agreed contribution value of ₦9,000. The contributor’s historical cost and previous depreciation belong to their old records.
questions.explanation: The partnership records the asset at the agreed contribution value of ₦9,000. The contributor’s historical cost and previous depreciation belong to their old records.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: When a partner makes a drawing of stock items from a partnership, the accounting impact of the drawing is to increase the partner’s

options.D: Profit and account credit loss balance.

questions.ai_explanation: A stock withdrawal for personal use is charged to the partner as drawings. Where current accounts are maintained, this increases the debit side and reduces the partner’s net entitlement.
questions.explanation: A stock withdrawal for personal use is charged to the partner as drawings. Where current accounts are maintained, this increases the debit side and reduces the partner’s net entitlement.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: Partnership appropriation: Kudu receives capital interest ₦750, salary ₦800 and profit share ₦3,300. Wale receives capital interest ₦550, salary ₦600 and profit share ₦3,300. Find net profit before appropriations.
questions.ai_explanation: Net profit before appropriations is the sum distributed as capital interest, salaries and residual profit. Add ₦750 + ₦550 + ₦800 + ₦600 + ₦3,300 + ₦3,300 = ₦9,300.
questions.explanation: Net profit before appropriations is the sum distributed as capital interest, salaries and residual profit. Add ₦750 + ₦550 + ₦800 + ₦600 + ₦3,300 + ₦3,300 = ₦9,300.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: Dele and Seun who are in partnership, have decided to convert their business into a limited liability company where both become directors. To convert the business

options.A: They will simply continue since there are no new members.
options.B: The partnership is formally ended and new company books opened.
options.C: The shares and all other items will be shared equally and not in their former ratios.
options.D: Computation of goodwill must b e done as it is legally required.

questions.ai_explanation: The company is a separate accounting entity. The partnership’s books must be closed and the company’s opening books established, even when the same people become directors.
questions.explanation: The company is a separate accounting entity. The partnership’s books must be closed and the company’s opening books established, even when the same people become directors.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: If a sole proprietorship is purchased for cash, then

options.A: The purchaser debits his business purchase account with the consideration he pays.
options.B: All assets and liabilities must be bought
options.C: Goodwill results where value liabilities taken is higher than the value of assets.
options.D: The vendor debits his businesspurchase account with the consideration he receives.

questions.ai_explanation: The purchaser records the agreed consideration as a debit to the business purchase account. Settlement credits cash; the acquired assets and liabilities are accounted for separately.
questions.explanation: The purchaser records the agreed consideration as a debit to the business purchase account. Settlement credits cash; the acquired assets and liabilities are accounted for separately.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: Zoom Plc reports paid-up capital ₦200,000, share premium ₦15,000 and retained profit ₦60,000. Find shareholders’ equity.
questions.ai_explanation: Shareholders’ equity comprises paid-up capital, share premium and retained profit. The sum is ₦200,000 + ₦15,000 + ₦60,000 = ₦275,000; creditors are excluded.
questions.explanation: Shareholders’ equity comprises paid-up capital, share premium and retained profit. The sum is ₦200,000 + ₦15,000 + ₦60,000 = ₦275,000; creditors are excluded.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: Calls in advance are treated in the balance sheet as
questions.ai_explanation: Calls in advance are money received before the related share call is due. Until called, the amount is treated as an obligation to the shareholder rather than called-up share capital.
questions.explanation: Calls in advance are money received before the related share call is due. Until called, the amount is treated as an obligation to the shareholder rather than called-up share capital.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: Shares issued to a vendour in payment of business purchased would require a debit to

options.A: Cash account and credit to share capital account
options.B: Share capital account and credit to vendor’s account

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: To record a stock transfer between departments, which accounts are debited and credited?

options.A: Debit goods outwards; credit goods inwards
options.C: Debit transferring department; credit receiving department
options.D: Debit receiving department; credit transferring department

questions.ai_explanation: The receiving department gains stock and is debited, while the transferring department gives up stock and is credited. The entries record the internal movement at the agreed transfer value.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: Under traditional fund accounting, a state government deducts employees’ insurance premiums for remittance to an insurer. In which fund are these deductions recorded?
questions.ai_explanation: Under traditional agency-fund accounting, employee deductions held for remittance belong to another party. They are accounted for in an agency fund, not as government operating revenue.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: Zaria owes ₦13,600, buys goods on credit for ₦69,000 and pays suppliers ₦51,600. A ₦3,000 payment cheque is returned unpaid and suppliers allow ₦1,500 discount. Find the closing amount owed.
questions.ai_explanation: Closing creditors equal ₦13,600 + ₦69,000 − ₦51,600 + ₦3,000 − ₦1,500 = ₦32,500. The returned cheque restores the debt previously treated as paid.
questions.explanation: Closing creditors equal ₦13,600 + ₦69,000 − ₦51,600 + ₦3,000 − ₦1,500 = ₦32,500. The returned cheque restores the debt previously treated as paid.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: When reconciling from the cash-book bank balance to the bank-statement balance, which item is added?
questions.ai_explanation: Unpresented cheques have already reduced the cash-book bank balance but not the statement balance. Adding them back when moving from cash book to bank statement reconciles that timing difference.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: Sales ₦20,000; cost of sales ₦10,000; operating expenses recorded ₦2,500, including prepaid expenses ₦500. Find net profit.
questions.ai_explanation: Gross profit is ₦20,000 − ₦10,000 = ₦10,000. Current-period expenses are ₦2,500 − ₦500 = ₦2,000, so net profit is ₦8,000.
questions.explanation: Gross profit is ₦20,000 − ₦10,000 = ₦10,000. Current-period expenses are ₦2,500 − ₦500 = ₦2,000, so net profit is ₦8,000.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: Sales ₦20,000; cost of sales ₦10,000; operating expenses recorded ₦2,500, including prepaid expenses ₦500. Find gross profit margin.
questions.ai_explanation: Gross profit is ₦10,000 on sales of ₦20,000. Gross margin uses sales as its denominator, giving ₦10,000/₦20,000 × 100 = 50%.
questions.explanation: Gross profit is ₦10,000 on sales of ₦20,000. Gross margin uses sales as its denominator, giving ₦10,000/₦20,000 × 100 = 50%.

questions.subject: accounts

options.A: Transactions systematically for routine managerial decision making.

options.C: Events clearly to facilitate strategic managerial decision-making

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: Which of the following errors will affect the trial balance totals?

options.B: Omission of one account from the list when extracting from the ledgers.
options.C: Failure to post sales of N 2,000 and purchases of N 2,000 from subsidiary ledgers.
options.D: Omission of sales of N 3,000 and purchase of N 2,000.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: An expense account is closed by a debit to

options.A: An asset account and credit to the expense account.
options.B: The expense account and a credit to an asset account.
options.C: Profit and loss account and a credit to the expense account.
options.D: The expense account and a credit to profit and loss account.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: Creditors control: opening debit balances ₦32,000 and credit balances ₦61,000; cash purchases ₦30,000; credit purchases ₦60,000; supplier payments ₦13,000 cash and ₦29,000 cheque; debtor contra ₦6,000. Find closing net creditors.
questions.ai_explanation: Start with net creditors ₦61,000 − ₦32,000 = ₦29,000. Add credit purchases ₦60,000 and subtract payments ₦42,000 and contra ₦6,000 to obtain ₦41,000.
questions.explanation: Start with net creditors ₦61,000 − ₦32,000 = ₦29,000. Add credit purchases ₦60,000 and subtract payments ₦42,000 and contra ₦6,000 to obtain ₦41,000.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: Factory costs: plant depreciation ₦1,600; rent ₦650; indirect wages ₦695; general indirect expenses ₦726; lubricants ₦1,235; power ₦350. Other costs: carriage inwards ₦829, bank charges ₦612 and carriage outwards ₦2,900. Find total factory overhead.
questions.ai_explanation: Factory overhead totals depreciation ₦1,600, rent ₦650, indirect wages ₦695, indirect expenses ₦726, lubricants ₦1,235 and power ₦350: ₦5,256. Exclude carriage and bank charges.
questions.explanation: Factory overhead totals depreciation ₦1,600, rent ₦650, indirect wages ₦695, indirect expenses ₦726, lubricants ₦1,235 and power ₦350: ₦5,256. Exclude carriage and bank charges.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: Shop cash book: paid suppliers ₦10,800; expenses ₦6,900; personal drawings ₦900; opening cash ₦15,750; closing cash ₦3,870; cash withdrawn from bank for the shop ₦1,720. Find receipts from debtors.
questions.ai_explanation: Receipts from debtors balance the cash account: payments ₦18,600 plus closing cash ₦3,870, less opening cash ₦15,750 and bank-to-shop transfer ₦1,720, give ₦5,000.
questions.explanation: Receipts from debtors balance the cash account: payments ₦18,600 plus closing cash ₦3,870, less opening cash ₦15,750 and bank-to-shop transfer ₦1,720, give ₦5,000.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: The items entered in an opening statement of affairs of an enterprise that keeps incomplete record are

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: Sales ledger: opening balance ₦10,600; debtor payments ₦32,275; credit sales ₦59,193; closing balance ₦20,751; discount allowed ₦2,890. Discount received elsewhere is ₦9,700. Find sales returns.
questions.ai_explanation: Sales returns equal opening debtors plus credit sales less collections, discount allowed and closing debtors: ₦10,600 + ₦59,193 − ₦32,275 − ₦2,890 − ₦20,751 = ₦13,877.
questions.explanation: Sales returns equal opening debtors plus credit sales less collections, discount allowed and closing debtors: ₦10,600 + ₦59,193 − ₦32,275 − ₦2,890 − ₦20,751 = ₦13,877.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: The simplest form of single entry procedure consist of keeping a

options.B: Cash book and ledger accounts showing debtors and creditors balances
options.C: Cash journal, sales journal and purchases journal
options.D: Day book in which transaction are described in chronological order.

questions.ai_explanation: A basic single-entry system commonly keeps a cash book plus personal accounts for debtors and creditors. It lacks the complete double-entry classification needed for all ledger balances.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: When a customer’s cheque is returned unpaid, what treatment is required in a debtors-control system, including the customer subsidiary ledger?

options.A: Debit bank; credit customer and control account
options.B: Credit bank; debit customer and control account
options.C: Debit customer; credit control account and bank
options.D: Credit control account; debit bank and customer

questions.explanation: Dishonour reverses the earlier receipt: credit bank and debit receivables control in the general ledger. Also debit the individual customer’s subsidiary account to restore the amount owed.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: Which of the following items does not feature in the balance sheet of a club?

options.B: Salary arrears paid in the current year
options.D: Advance subscription in respect of a coming year.

questions.ai_explanation: Salary arrears already paid are no longer outstanding liabilities. Subscription arrears remain receivables, while advance rent and subscriptions remain liabilities at the reporting date.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: An outright sale of partnership amounts to the

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: Maimalari Ltd has earnings per share of 30 kobo, nominal value ₦1.20 and market price ₦1.50 per share. Find its earnings yield.

questions.subject: accounts
questions.question: When valuing a purchased business at an unchanged purchase consideration, which effect follows from increasing the value assigned to its assets?

questions.question: Closing fixed-asset cost ₦3,100,000; disposals cost ₦900,000 with accumulated depreciation ₦150,000; additions cost ₦100,000. Accumulated depreciation opens at ₦350,000 and closes at ₦300,000. Find opening fixed-asset cost.
